description:
Send to and receive from the person: completions, updates, questions, answers to questions addressed to you, withdrawals, and what a question holds up. Every Goal named must exist: an unknown one refuses the whole contact. Each item applies on its own: read `results`, where a failed one names why.

HOW TO ASK:
1. One question per object in `questions`, so each is answered on its own.
2. `goalId` names the existing Goal it is about (create one with manage_goals first); the answer comes back there.
3. `workItBlocks` only when you are truly blocked: it asks for a call.
4. No while-loops. While any Call is open, even one your question joined from their items, keep receiving through empty windows; otherwise stop at one: the answer reaches you on the Goal. Yield only with a listener or wakeup.
5. One question, one row: never re-send one still waiting; take back one that no longer matters with `withdrawQuestionIds`.
6. Read the Goal before asking; never re-ask what was answered or shipped. `replied` means they chose no option: it is still yours to settle.
7. Give options when you have them. Each label names its choice in full (never "Option 2"); never add "Other". `pickMode`: one (default), many, rank.
8. A diagnosis says when, why and how it happens, then proposes one fix.
9. Give a report its `reply`: one line in THEIR voice for THAT report, so you learn whether they verified it or only received it. Required when it is delivered or its Goal is done.

LENGTH: the question, message or answer is the one point, at most 80 characters; the rest goes in `units`, one idea each. Over a cap is refused by name and nothing is sent. Several results are several updates.

UPDATES ask nothing. One reaches the person only when they asked for it, it answers something they said, or its Goal is done; else it is kept as progress. One that reaches them joins an open report card or a live call.

RECEIVING: contact({}) waits ~45 s; contact({wait:false}) returns `events` at once. Confirm the ones you handled with contact({ackEventIds}).

ackEventIds.description: The exact eventIds of the events you have handled: an acknowledgment (ACK). Reading alone acknowledges nothing, so an event comes back until you acknowledge it; after that the next batch can come. Each recipient acknowledges separately, for itself only. A Question you owe is answered (answers), never acknowledged away.

answers.description: Answers to Questions addressed to you.

selectedOptionIds.description: The ids of the options you choose, when the Question offered options (in order, for a ranking).

text.description: Your answer in your own words, at most 80 characters; the context goes in units.

questionId.description: The Question you answer: its id as the event or the conversation shows it (8 characters or whole).

units.description: The context this message needs, as up to 12 units in reading order, each {title, body}: a title of at most 50 characters and a body of at most 200. One idea per unit: context they may open, never something they must hear. Leave it out when the main text says it all. Over a cap is refused by name (ask_too_long, too_many_units, unit_title_too_long, unit_body_too_long) and nothing is sent.

body.description: The unit itself, at most 200 characters.

title.description: What this unit is about, at most 50 characters. The app lists the titles; the person taps one to read its body.

bumpQuestionIds.description: Your own questions still waiting on the person that you want them to notice again. Each moves back to the top of its card with one new notification; nothing is resent and no second card is made.

completions.description: COMPLETIONS close and report in one operation, the same contract as manage_goals kind:complete: closure and the report commit together or neither does. Required children and dependencies must already be finished. options suggest next steps: a tap acknowledges the report and requests that step, and never reopens the Goal (follow-up work needs a new one). No reviewer rejudges it: say only what your evidence supports. Ordinary updates never close a Goal.

causedBy.description: The person's own words this acts on: the ids (or the short ids get_goals prints) of their answers or notes that led to it, at most 10. Their app shows each result under the words that caused it, so name every one this follows from. An id that is not their words is refused by name (cause_not_found, cause_ambiguous) and nothing is written.

message.description: Completion headline, at most 50 characters: the one thing that would go wrong or stay unclear later if they missed it.

options.description: Optional next steps the person may initiate: label (50 characters) and consequence in hint (200). Selecting one acknowledges the report and requests that step from its author; it never reopens this Goal.

reply.description: One acknowledgement in the person's voice, at most 50 characters. Acknowledgement alone requests no follow-up and does not claim they tested the work.

shipped.description: Only when this reports a result that LANDED somewhere the person can see it: phone (an app update reached their phone), calls (the voice bot), server, store (the App Store) or agents (the MCP or SDK). Leave it out for work in progress.

units.description: Suggest initial state, changes, current state with verification and limits, and next steps / leftover work with its owner when useful. One idea per unit; omit unnecessary sections.

questionDependencies.description: Add or remove what a Question you asked holds up, after asking it.

action.description: What waits: starting or completing a Goal, or answering a Question.

blocked.description: A Goal or a Question, by its id.

reason.description: Why, as an explanation, never as policy.

questions.description: Questions for the person, one per object, each sent exactly as written, with no reading in between.

goalId.description: The Goal the question is about, which must exist (create it with manage_goals first). Its answer comes back there.

options.description: The choices, when you have them. Each label stands on its own and differs from the others (duplicate_option_label), at most 50 characters; a hint, at most 200. They can always answer in their own words, so no 'Other' or 'None of these'.

hint.description: Optional: what choosing it does, at most 200 characters (e.g. 'Reruns test suite', 'Merges to main').

htmlPreview.description: Optional sandboxed HTML/CSS preview for a visual 'pick one' (shown in the option card). Untrusted-sandboxed: NO JavaScript, NO external network or images — inline CSS and data: URIs only; <=16KB. Rendered edge-to-edge in a responsive card that is 200pt tall (about 320pt wide on a phone, with the next option peeking beside it); make your HTML fit that viewport. Use for layout/CSS mockups, tables, diffs. For a hosted image use the image URL instead.

id.description: Optional: this option's own id, which answers name it by (selectedOptionIds). Give every option one, or none: without them the options are numbered "1", "2", … in order.

imgUrl.description: Optional image URL rendered as the option's preview (plain image, not sandboxed). For agent-generated HTML/CSS mockups, use the HTML preview instead.

label.description: The choice, at most 50 characters, standing on its own.

pickMode.description: How the options are answered: "one" (the default) a pick, for alternatives; "many" a checklist, for independent options they may want several of; "rank" an order of all of them. Only with options; "many" and "rank" need at least two (too_few_options).

question.description: ONE question, in at most 80 characters, and only what is needed to answer it; the context goes in units. Several questions are several objects, one each: an answer settles the one question it was given, so a person who answers the part of a bundled question that interested them settles nothing and is asked again. Separate questions cost nothing: ANY contact for a person already on a call JOINS that call, so several arrive as one call.

questionId.description: Optional: your own stable id for this question (a UUID), so a resend is the same question. Minted for you when omitted; the result returns it.

units.description: The context this message needs, as up to 12 units in reading order, each {title, body}: a title of at most 50 characters and a body of at most 200. One idea per unit: context they may open, never something they must hear. Leave it out when the main text says it all. Over a cap is refused by name (ask_too_long, too_many_units, unit_title_too_long, unit_body_too_long) and nothing is sent.

body.description: The unit itself, at most 200 characters.

title.description: What this unit is about, at most 50 characters. The app lists the titles; the person taps one to read its body.

userExplicitlyRequested.description: Only what the person said about THIS message, in so many words: "any" when they asked you to send it to them ("send it to my phone", "message me the result"), "call" when they asked to be called about it. It is then delivered (a call rings for the whole contact, and carries everything waiting on them); omitted, an update is only recorded as the Goal's progress unless the person needs it. Never set it to make a message louder.

workItBlocks.description: The work that cannot go on until this is answered: a Goal's start or completion, or another Question's answer. Only for work truly blocked; it asks for a call. Leave it out for a question you can keep working around.

action.description: What waits: starting or completing a Goal, or answering a Question.

blocked.description: A Goal or a Question, by its id.

reason.description: Why, as an explanation, never as policy.

updates.description:
News: progress, findings, a result. An update asks nothing. It reaches the person only when they asked for it (userExplicitlyRequested), when it answers something they said, or once its Goal is done; otherwise it is recorded as the Goal's progress, which the person is not told. Every update reaches the other agents that wrote on its Goal in the last hour: to tell another agent something, write it as an update on that agent's Goal, with its `kind`.

ONE LOAD-BEARING POINT PER REPORT: the message is the point they must not miss; a second point that would go wrong or stay unclear later if they missed it is its own update, never a unit.

causedBy.description: The person's own words this acts on: the ids (or the short ids get_goals prints) of their answers or notes that led to it, at most 10. Their app shows each result under the words that caused it, so name every one this follows from. An id that is not their words is refused by name (cause_not_found, cause_ambiguous) and nothing is written.

goalIds.description: The Goals it is about, each one that exists: the one it is mainly about first.

kind.description: What an agent writing on ANOTHER agent's Goal expects of its reader, as one token: handing, replaced-by <goalId>, blocked-by <goalId|questionId>, asking, found. `handing` the work is yours now, nothing is asked; `replaced-by <goalId>` this Goal is dead and that one carries its work; `blocked-by <goalId|questionId>` I cannot go on until that moves, no action unless you own it; `found` evidence on your Goal, nothing is asked and nothing has changed. `asking` is a question, so it belongs in `questions`, not here. It is written for the other agents on the Goal, never the person, so it does not go with userExplicitlyRequested; leave it out for your own progress. Refused by name (kind_unknown, kind_needs_id, kind_takes_no_id, kind_is_a_question, kind_not_for_the_person).

message.description: The one point, at most 80 characters: the one thing that would go wrong or stay unclear later if they missed it, said as what changed for them, in their words ("The screen reader speaks Spanish too", not "Merged #3896"). A second point like that is its own update; the rest goes in units.

reply.description: What this report's button says instead of "Got it", at most 50 characters, written in THEIR voice for THIS report ("Sounds good, I'll test later") -- the care you give a question's options, so what they tap tells you whether they verified your work or only received it. One tap sends exactly these words back to you. Words that would CHANGE what happens next are a question, not a reply to a report: it still asks nothing and still owes you no answer. The reply is required for requested delivery and completed Goals; ordinary progress may omit it.

shipped.description: Only when this reports a result that LANDED somewhere the person can see it: phone (an app update reached their phone), calls (the voice bot), server, store (the App Store) or agents (the MCP or SDK). Leave it out for work in progress.

units.description: The context this message needs, as up to 12 units in reading order, each {title, body}: a title of at most 50 characters and a body of at most 200. One idea per unit: context they may open, never something they must hear. Leave it out when the main text says it all. Over a cap is refused by name (ask_too_long, too_many_units, unit_title_too_long, unit_body_too_long) and nothing is sent.

body.description: The unit itself, at most 200 characters.

title.description: What this unit is about, at most 50 characters. The app lists the titles; the person taps one to read its body.

userExplicitlyRequested.description: Only what the person said about THIS message, in so many words: "any" when they asked you to send it to them ("send it to my phone", "message me the result"), "call" when they asked to be called about it. It is then delivered (a call rings for the whole contact, and carries everything waiting on them); omitted, an update is only recorded as the Goal's progress unless the person needs it. Never set it to make a message louder.

wait.description: Only controls when this returns. Sending: false (the default) returns at once; true waits up to about 45 seconds for a response to what you sent. Sending nothing: true (the default) waits up to about 45 seconds for anything addressed to you; false returns what is waiting now. It does not mean work is blocked, set urgency, or ask for a call. `waitOutcome` says which happened: `available`, `expired` (nothing arrived; wait again without sending again), or `not_waited`.

withdrawQuestionIds.description: Questions you asked that no longer need an answer: you acted on them yourself, they no longer matter, or you asked wrongly. Each is cancelled, not answered: its card closes and nothing rings for it.

name: contact
title: Contact the person
